verdict: Alphabet grew revenue 14% to $84.7B as Search rose 14% and Google Cloud jumped 29% — and it kept $23.6B as profit, even after a $714M paper loss on its investment stakes.

segments.name: Google Services
segments.note: Search, YouTube, subscriptions and devices — Search & other revenue rose 14% to $48.5B and YouTube ads 13% to $8.7B.

segments.name: Google Cloud
segments.note: Cloud computing rented to companies — up 29%, and its operating profit nearly tripled to $1.2B from $0.4B a year ago.

segments.name: Other Bets
segments.note: Moonshot projects such as Waymo — small revenue and a $1.1B operating loss this quarter.

segments.name: Hedging gains
segments.note: Gains from currency hedging that sit outside the three businesses.

opex.name: Research & development
opex.note: Engineers and researchers building the products and AI models.

opex.name: Sales & marketing
opex.note: Selling ads and devices, and promoting the products.

opex.name: General & administrative
opex.note: Running the company — legal, finance and facilities.

otherDetail: Interest income of $1,090M and a $128M performance-fee reversal, partly offset by a $714M loss on equity securities, a $310M loss on debt securities, currency losses and interest expense, net.
follow100Note: A $714M paper loss on investments is netted inside the $0.15 of other income per $100. The rows may not add exactly due to rounding.

takeaways.title: Cloud is compounding
takeaways.text: Google Cloud revenue jumped 29% to $10.3B, and its operating profit nearly tripled to $1.2B from $0.4B a year ago — the cloud has become a real second engine, not just a growth story.

takeaways.title: Search still pays for everything
takeaways.text: Search & other revenue rose 14% to $48.5B and YouTube ads grew 13% to $8.7B — the advertising core still supplies the great bulk of Alphabet's money.

takeaways.title: Profit rose 29%
takeaways.text: Net income rose 29% to $23.6B despite the $714M paper loss on equity investments inside other income; free cash flow was $13.5B in the quarter.

oneTimers: A $714M loss on equity securities — paper losses on stakes Alphabet holds — is netted inside the small $126M of net other income; together with a $128M reversal of previously accrued performance fees, it cut net income by $463M (about $0.04 a share), per the release's own footnote.
